about: Mission control (doc 102). The commander's intent, the crew (every role an AI agent until scope or revenue needs a person), the decisions kept for the owner, the flight rules, and the twelve management disciplines mapped onto the estate. governance/mission.py reads it; governance/tests/test_mission.py checks every command named here exists.
intent: Keep the owner's data safe and the estate useful every day, at the lowest cost in money, machine and attention; when unsure, protect the data and wait.
owner_decides: spending money, opening or closing an outside account, anything that cannot be undone (deleting data, rotating the backup key, publishing), and a red security finding's risk acceptance

crew.does: runs the loop: reads the board, applies the flight rules, writes postmortems
keeps the estate up, backed up, current and within its disk
writes the fix or the feature from a brief
a second, independent look before anything merges
keeps the KRIs, the risk register and the crisis plans current, and says what is over appetite
maps every obligation to a control, evidence and an owner; watches the regulators
independently checks that what is claimed is true: tests, drills, proof gaps, restore drills
what is changing outside: regulators, threats, prices
tells the owner only what needs the owner, and the weekly progress

flight_rules.then: an update runs only when every Go/No-Go console says GO
freeze updates and off-site copies; you check the alarm (./securax continuity show data-lost)
clean what the storage rules allow, then report what is left
answers are guessing: add a stronger model (./securax keys), or let careful mode answer important questions
the strong model is being skipped: check the provider chain
a key behaves unusually: you decide whether to revoke it (./securax gateway-auth key list)
a regulator's reporting clock is running: the incident page says what is due and when
